newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Dlr vols a touch firmer in line with spot.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Dlr vols a touch firmer in line with spot.

text.p: Implied volatilities in dollar/mark and dollar/yen options were slightly higher as spot dollar perked up, but moves were limited as the spot rates were still in familiar ranges.

Dollar/mark volatilities were firmer after the spot rate rose three pfennigs from a one-month low on Monday, and was quoted at 1.8383 marks at 1120 GMT against its late Monday European level of 1.8355.
One-month vols were at 11.60/00 percent against 11.50/80 yesterday.
Demand for calls and puts were biased slightly towards dollar puts, with 25-delta risk reversals at -0.05/2.0 against around par yesterday.

Traders said the market was bracing for key events later this week, namely the Federal Open Market Committee meeting today and the Bundesbank's council meeting, its first after a four-week summer break, on Thursday.
Although the market does not expect rate changes in either the U.S. or Germany this week it would, as always, be on the lookout for any hints on interest rate direction or currencies, they said.
Dollar/yen vols also ticked higher as the spot rate rose above 118 yen overnight, putting a key target of 120 yen back on the horizon and creating concerns about near-term volatility.

"Dollar/yen's climbing, albeit slowly, and this is making it difficult for vols to go down, because once it gets nearer 120, the market could either knock it down sharply or make it sail through 120," said Yoshiaki Yamamoto, options dealer at Sakura Bank in London.
One-month dollar/yen vols were quoted at 12.50/80 percent against late Monday's 12.40/70.
The spot dollar/yen rate was at 118.10/20 against 117.95 in late trade yesterday.
Market demand stayed in favour of yen puts, with risk reversals unchanged from Monday at 0.2/0.5.
Volatilities in mark/yen, meanwhile, settled down as the market noticed a slowdown in spot mark's aggressive rebound against the yen after hitting a 25-month low last week.

"It's true vols haven't changed much today and seem to have calmed down for now, but they're still almost equal to those of dollar/mark and dollar/yen, which are very high levels (for mark/yen)," Sakura's Yamamoto said.
One-month mark/yen vols were at 11.70/12.00 percent against yesterday's 11.80/12.10, with risk reversals at around par.
In sterling volatilities, there was not much incentive to buy up vols with spot sterling/mark and cable stuck in familiar ranges, traders said.
Sterling/mark vols were at 11.60/12.00 percent against Monday's 11.80/12.00, and cable vols at 10.20/40 against 10.30/70.
